key_insight: The paper enforces Dirichlet boundary velocities strongly in port-Hamiltonian elastodynamics by using a lifting-based kinematic decomposition, avoiding DAE constraints while preserving energy structure.
engineering_relevance: This gives finite element practitioners an ODE-based alternative to Lagrange multipliers or weak imposition, improving boundary accuracy for structure-preserving solid mechanics simulations.
method: Split displacement/velocity into a boundary-vanishing dynamic part plus a prescribed lifting field.
Embed the lifting map in virtual power principles to obtain lifted port-Hamiltonian models.
Derive both 2-field and 4-field FEM formulations and show equivalence to standard matrix partitioning under special shape functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations that verify energy-balance properties and computational performance of the proposed formulations.
watch_item: The lifting field and associated discrete mapping must be chosen carefully, since poor construction could affect accuracy, implementation complexity, or equivalence to standard FEM.
paper_title: Strong imposition of Dirichlet boundary velocities in structure-preserving discretizations of elastodynamics
